work.title: Disputation between the Apostle Peter and Nero
work.edition: Machine translation (gpt-6.1-sol, Patristica, 2026-10-28) of: Paul Bedjan Acta martyrum et sanctorum 2; TEI by J. E. Walters, Digital Syriac Corpus (syriaccorpus.org 524)

paragraphs.text: [?] of Saint Peter and King Nero.

I looked out over the troubled sea and saw twelve ships sailing. The sea had risen against them, but he passed through it and calmed its waves. He set the sea’s four winds in order, for their pilot was wise. However much it rose and raged, they showed their victory. The sea’s waves rose high, so that the ships might sink in them. But they kept their course straight, reached the harbor, and rested. From here: salted provisions [?]; helps. And let us all together, with one accord, offer glory to the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. May his compassion overshadow our whole congregation, every one of us, now and at all times and forever and ever.

They carried great wealth and distributed it without limit. The king of the sea saw their wealth and stirred up the sea so that they would sink in it. The sea is this world, and the ships are the twelve apostles in it. The sea that rose against them is the world that rejected their teaching. I called the evil one the king of the sea: the enemy of Jesus and his servants. I called the kingdom the harbor, for the apostles found rest within it. When the enemy saw the apostles proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, he led the judges of the world astray so that they would not accept their good news. He found himself an eager servant, Nero Caesar, and was pleased with him. Through him he fulfilled his desire against two apostles, Simon Peter and Paul. The Paraclete, who comforts everyone, had sent Simon to Rome, where Nero was reigning—a field that produced thorns. Paul, the herald of the nations, traveled to Rome to join his senior fellow worker [?]. Nero heard their teaching and armed himself for debate. Nero. Nero said to his servants, roused by his fury: “What have you heard, my friends? That Galileans have come up to our city!” Servants. “May you live forever, O king! The report you have heard is true. They are indeed going about in our city, teaching the Nazarene’s doctrine.” Nero. “In what guise do they appear, and what is their teaching, that they dared to come and were not overcome by the gods who overcome everyone?” Servant. Order, my lord the king, that they come here, and hear what they have to say, for there is no way of life like theirs.

And their teaching is foreign to the world. Nero: A great calamity has come upon us! Perhaps our gods will be abolished, and their temples too will be overthrown. What shall we do if this happens? Servants: It is a great disgrace, as you have said, since all nations tremble before you. If two men defeat you, it is a great disgrace throughout the world! Nero: Go and bring them here to me, so that I may hear what they have to say. For if they do not worship our gods, they shall be cut apart limb by limb. Servants: It is our duty to obey you and bring the men you told us about. They hurried off joyfully and brought them to stand before his throne. Nero: Are these the men who have disturbed us and thrown mighty Rome into turmoil? Come forward and explain your teaching to me. And who sent you to come here? Simon: Look, O king, if you had learned from the teaching of the one who sent me, you would not be ruling only on earth; in heaven too your throne would [?]. Nero: Who is this who sent you, whose authority is greater than mine? If you are his envoy, the king you serve is contemptible. Simon: Do not look at me as insignificant, and do not look down on the simplicity of my words. Look at the signs of the one who sent me, which condemn your teaching. Nero: Go away, old man! You are greatly mistaken. Leave our city, to which you have come. Who sent you to come here—the one you rely on and boast about? Simon: The time for me to leave has not yet come, until I have cultivated your city and uprooted the thorns within it,

and sown my Lord’s seed within it. Nero: Look, old man, you are greatly mistaken, for you have called Zeus and his companions thorns. On whom do you rely, that you insult the gods of great Rome? Simon: See, O king, how despised I am: even my words are unwelcome to you. For we who are despised before your throne, through the signs that are seen [?]. Nero: I have heard the report that the people of Jerusalem hung that Lord of yours on a tree. And if it is true, as they say, he was laid in a tomb like everyone else. Simon: The report you have heard is true: he was laid in a tomb like everyone else. And he rose from the tomb unharmed, and ascended to the highest heavens and took his seat. Nero: I offer you two gifts: death and life, two brothers. If you deny him, gain life; and if you do not deny him, taste death. Peter: Jesus taught us and told us, “Whoever denies me, I will deny him. And whoever acknowledges me in this world, I will honor him in the kingdom of heaven.” Nero: Deny the Christ whom you proclaim, and I will honor you in Rome. Do not contend against my kingdom and lead mighty Rome astray. Simon: You have clothed yourself in zeal for the king against that King who made me king. Do you not know, wretched man, that the heights and the depths hang upon his command? Nero: Did not Herod seek to kill him, the one of whom you say, “He made me king”? And if the Egyptians had not sheltered him, he would not have remained

in the world. Peter: Have you not heard, Nero, what overtook Herod? Severe and varied torments—and so he departed from the world. Nero: What sense is there in our being persuaded by you, accepting your words, and believing you? How can someone who did not save himself give life to others? Peter: Death, which ruled over our race—he undid it and abolished it through his resurrection. He plundered the treasury of Sheol and shut the mouth of the devourer. Nero: Let your Lord come and rescue you when I order you to be crucified. And if he is true, as you say, let everyone know that he has authority over me. Simon: Let Pilate arise and refute you, the one in whose court he stood and was tried. For he washed his hands of his blood, knowing that he was Lord of all. Nero: Foolish old man, do you not know that your death and your life lie hidden in my hands? Why have you dared to insult me? Do you not know that your end has come? Simon: I am an old man, as you said, and the Lord who chose me sent me to be a father and instruct everyone, and to turn everyone toward the Lord. Nero: Is it only to us that you have been sent, or do you preach to all nations? And if it is Rome that you have reached, you are not accepted even in Rome. Peter: All the nations that are scattered—twelve men give them counsel. And Rome fell to me as my allotted portion, from the Holy Spirit who sent me. Nero.

So Paul, as you said, is with you, preaching. And has great and mighty Rome fallen to you two alone as your portion? Peter. Paul has been assigned to the Gentiles alone, to preach, teach, and admonish. And the Lord has authorized him to convert the nations everywhere. Nero. You were a fisherman, as people say, but you abandoned the fishing you grew up with. And you chose another trade, one that destroys your [?]. Simon. Fishing for fish brought me no profit; I have been appointed to catch people. And now I catch people so that they may become servants of the one who sent me. Nero. If you had bowed down for a little while, you could have gone on living in the world. But now that you have acted boldly and have not feared me, your life in this world is coming to an end. Peter. Our Lord warned us beforehand: “Do not be shaken, my friends, by those who kill the body but cannot destroy your souls.” Nero. Rome has been the capital of our kingdom: [?] every death by which you will die. Simon. As you said, mighty Rome is the capital of your kingdom. I have sown good seed in it. Give me a cross as the reward for my labor. Nero. A fine reward you have asked of me—the cross on which your master too was crucified! Let my sword be Paul’s reward, and I will honor you with a cross. Simon. Listen and grant me one request: when my Lord was crucified, his head was upward.

Let my head be downward and my feet upward, for I am not worthy to be crucified like my Lord. The spectators stood marveling at the courageous and faithful old man. “Well done, Peter!” the believers cried. “How firm your foundation is!” “Let thanks be given to the Good One,” the believers cried, “for your name has been [?] in our dwelling place. And may the bones of your apostles also be advocates for your faithful.”
